name: Munroe Island (Munrothuruthu)
tagline: A quiet cluster of canals, coir and village life where Kallada meets Ashtamudi
summary: Munroe Island (Munrothuruthu) is a small cluster of backwater islets in Kollam where the Kallada River meets Ashtamudi Lake, known for narrow canals, coir craft and intimate village cruises.
description: Munroe Island (locally Munrothuruthu or Mundrothuruth) is a cluster of tiny islets at the confluence of the Kallada River and Ashtamudi Lake in Kollam district. The low-lying islands and narrow canals create an intimate backwater landscape of coconut groves, paddy patches, mangrove fringes and village lanes.

The place matters for its living backwater culture: traditional coir retting and weaving, small-scale fishing and prawn farming, canoe and kayak canals, and a way of life shaped by tidal water and seasonal floods. Visitors see close-up village routines rather than big tourist infrastructure.

Munroe Island also faces environmental stress — shoreline erosion, rising water levels, salinity intrusion and damage from past floods — which shapes how tourism and conservation projects work here. Responsible, low-impact visits and local community programmes form the current approach to tourism.
highlights: Scenic narrow-canal cruises and canoe/kayak trips
Traditional coir retting and weaving demonstrations
Quiet village walks, birdwatching and mangrove patches
Local homestays and small backwater operators
Photogenic waterways and sunset views over Ashtamudi

sections.heading: Background
body: Munroe Island is a group of eight small islets formed where the Kallada River debouches into Ashtamudi Lake. The name comes from Colonel John Munroe, a 19th‑century Resident of Travancore linked with canal works in the region.

Historically the islands rely on coir, fishing and aquaculture; the landscape and livelihoods are tightly linked to tidal water flow and sedimentation. Scientific and government studies note ongoing erosion, salinity intrusion and inundation risks, which local plans and tourism initiatives try to address.

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Take a slow country boat or canoe cruise through the narrow canals to see coconut groves, coir retting pits, fishermen at work and small hamlets opening onto the water. Kayaking and guided village walks give closer contact with daily life.

Watch or learn about coir-making and small-scale aquaculture, visit mangrove fringes and look for resident and migratory birds. Photography, sunset cruises on Ashtamudi and staying in family-run homestays are the main visitor experiences.

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Munroe Island lies within easy reach of Kollam city and is best experienced as a day trip or an overnight homestay. Boat cruises and DTPC/community boat services operate from Kollam and nearby jetties; private operators and responsible‑tourism trails also run village experience programmes.

Keep realistic expectations: facilities are low-key, water levels change with seasons and some local ferry links have been disrupted at times. Confirm boat and ferry services, homestay availability and any guided activity before you travel.

latest.text: Kerala state budget earmarks ₹2 crore (2026–27) for Munroe Island development with emphasis on conservation and backwater tourism.
Kerala Tourism's Responsible Tourism 'Life Experience Trails' lists Munroe Island programmes (seasonal village trails and canal cruises) for Oct–Dec 2026.
News reports note visitor numbers recovering after a lull and renewed local interest in small-group backwater visits (May 2026).
Local reporting documents suspension of the Kavanad–Sambranikodi ferry route earlier in 2026; boat/ferry links can affect local access—confirm before travel.

visitorInfo.bestTime: October–March (cool, dry months; calm backwaters and clear skies).
visitorInfo.howToReach: Reach Kollam by train or road, then take a local boat/cruise or road+short boat transfer to Munroe Island (Kerala Tourism notes it is roughly 25–30 km from Kollam town). There is a small railway halt (Munroturuttu/Munrothuruthu) and local ferries—confirm schedules before travel.
etiquette: Book homestays and guided canal or kayak trips in advance; many offerings are small, community run.
Carry sunscreen, mosquito repellent and waterproof protection for cameras—water levels and weather vary.
Respect private property and village life: ask before photographing people or entering courtyards.
Confirm boat/ferry timings and inquire locally about any seasonal access disruptions before your trip.
